root_cause.text: The Bluetooth hci_le_create_big_complete_evt() function iterates BT_BOUND BIG connections without validating that the loop index stays below ev->num_bis, so it can read past the flexible bis_handle[] array and leave the same connection in BT_BOUND state, causing repeated lookup and an infinite loop.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “there is no check that i stays within ev->num_bis before the array access,” and the patch adds `if (ev->num_bis <= i)` before `ev->bis_handle[i++]`, plus error handling/termination when handle assignment fails because otherwise the connection “remains in BT_BOUND state” and is found again by `hci_conn_hash_lookup_big_state()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Bluetooth hci_le_create_big_complete_evt() function iterates BT_BOUND BIG connections without validating that the loop index stays below ev->num_bis, so it can read past the flexible bis_handle[] array and leave the same connection in BT_BOUND state, causing repeated lookup and an infinite loop.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states “there is no check that i stays within ev->num_bis before the array access,” and the patch adds `if (ev->num_bis <= i)` before `ev->bis_handle[i++]`, plus error handling/termination when handle assignment fails because otherwise the connection “remains in BT_BOUND state” and is found again by `hci_conn_hash_lookup_big_state()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix BIG creation handling by detecting missing or unassignable BIS handles and failing the affected BIS connection instead of continuing with invalid setup.
intent_record.what: The change adds two new error-handling branches in hci_le_create_big_complete_evt(): one checks whether ev->num_bis is less than or equal to the current BIS index i before accessing ev->bis_handle[i], and another wraps hci_conn_set_handle(...) in a conditional so that if setting the BIS handle fails, an error is logged. In both cases, the code now logs a BIG-specific error message, sets ev->status to HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED, calls hci_connect_cfm(conn, ev->status), deletes the connection with hci_conn_del(conn), and continues to the next iteration.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the code from reading past the available BIS handles when fewer handles are reported than expected, and it ensures that failures to assign a BIS handle are treated as connection setup failures. Instead of proceeding with an invalid or incomplete BIG/BIS setup, the affected connection is explicitly failed and removed so the BIG can be terminated when not all BIS links are successfully connected.

intent_record.intent_summary: Terminate the BIG when create completion returns an unspecified error, as well as when no BIS connections were established, to properly clean up failed BIG creation.
intent_record.what: The condition controlling BIG termination in hci_le_create_big_complete_evt() was changed from `if (!ev->status && !i)` to `if (ev->status == HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED || (!ev->status && !i))`, and a new comment was added explaining that the BIG should be terminated either on an unexpected error or when no BISes were connected.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now also terminates the BIG when the create BIG complete event reports `HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED`, instead of only terminating when creation succeeded but zero BISes were connected. This adds handling for an unexpected error path so the BIG is cleaned up rather than left active or inconsistent.

grouping_result.intent: Fix BIG creation handling by detecting missing or unassignable BIS handles and failing the affected BIS connection instead of continuing with invalid setup.
Terminate the BIG when create completion returns an unspecified error, as well as when no BIS connections were established, to properly clean up failed BIG creation.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets BIG creation completion handling and specifically adds failure handling when BIS handles are missing or cannot be assigned, which is directly tied to the root cause of iterating BIG/BIS connections without proper validation and leaving connections stuck in BT_BOUND state.

The change handles cleanup of failed BIG creation on unspecified error or zero BIS establishment, but it does not address the root cause: missing bounds validation of the loop index against ev->num_bis leading to out-of-bounds bis_handle[] access and an infinite loop.

candidates.rationale: This statement consumes ev->bis_handle[i++] without validating that i is still less than ev->num_bis. That directly matches the root cause: out-of-bounds access to the flexible bis_handle array while iterating BT_BOUND BIG connections.

When handle assignment fails, execution continues without transitioning or failing the affected connection, allowing it to remain in BT_BOUND state and be found again on later iterations, contributing to the repeated lookup/infinite loop behavior described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement reads from ev->bis_handle using i++ without validating that the index remains below ev->num_bis. That is the direct out-of-bounds read described in the root cause when iterating BT_BOUND BIG connections.

When BIS handle assignment fails, this continue leaves the same connection in BT_BOUND state instead of failing or transitioning it. That allows repeated lookup of the same connection on subsequent iterations, contributing to the infinite-loop behavior tied to the missing bis_handle bounds validation.

    Bluetooth: hci_conn: Fix modifying handle while aborting
    
    This introduces hci_conn_set_handle which takes care of verifying the
    conditions where the hci_conn handle can be modified, including when
    hci_conn_abort has been called and also checks that the handles is
    valid as well.
    
    Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function body is shown, so this is sufficient to assess the specific root cause. In hci_le_create_big_complete_evt(), the loop iterates matching BT_BOUND connections using `list_for_each_entry_rcu(conn, &hdev->conn_hash.list, list)` and for each match assigns `__le16_to_cpu(ev->bis_handle[i++])` via `hci_conn_set_handle(conn, __le16_to_cpu(ev->bis_handle[i++]))`. There is still no check that `i` remains less than `ev->num_bis` before indexing `ev->bis_handle[i]`. That matches the described root cause: iteration over bound BIG connections without validating the loop index against `ev->num_bis`, allowing out-of-bounds reads from the flexible `bis_handle[]` array. The introduced helper `hci_conn_set_handle(...)` only validates whether the handle may be set / is valid; it does not bound-check the BIS array index. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix for this vulnerability is not present in this commit.

Bluetooth: ISO: Add support for connecting multiple BISes

It is required for some configurations to have multiple BISes
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a0bfde167b506423111ddb8cd71930497a40fc54
Author: Iulia Tanasescu <iulia.tanasescu@nxp.com>
Date:   Tue May 30 17:21:59 2023 +0300

    Bluetooth: ISO: Add support for connecting multiple BISes
    
    It is required for some configurations to have multiple BISes as part
    of the same BIG.
    
    Similar to the flow implemented for unicast, DEFER_SETUP will also be
    used to bind multiple BISes for the same BIG, before starting Periodic
    Advertising and creating the BIG.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full iteration and indexing logic introduced by this commit. The vulnerable construct is present in the loop over all matching bound BIG connections: `list_for_each_entry_rcu(conn, &hdev->conn_hash.list, list) { ... conn->handle = __le16_to_cpu(ev->bis_handle[bis_idx++]); ... }`. There is no check that `bis_idx` remains less than `ev->num_bis` before reading `ev->bis_handle[bis_idx++]`. Since `ev->bis_handle` is a flexible array whose valid entries are limited by `ev->num_bis`, this can read past the end when more matching BT_BOUND connections are encountered than BIS handles reported in the event. The root-cause condition described is therefore present: iteration over bound BIG connections without validating the loop index against `ev->num_bis`. The fix is not present because there is no guard such as `if (bis_idx >= ev->num_bis)` or equivalent handling to stop/skip excess connections before indexing the array.

ISO events (CIS/BIS) shall only be relevant

Date:   Mon Sep 19 11:10:17 2022 -0700

    Bluetooth: hci_event: Make sure ISO events don't affect non-ISO connections
    
    ISO events (CIS/BIS) shall only be relevant for connection with link
    type of ISO_LINK, otherwise the controller is probably buggy or it is
    the result of fuzzer tools such as syzkaller.
    
    Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The provided snippet is sufficient because it shows the body of `hci_le_create_big_complete_evt()` around the relevant logic. The root cause is lack of bounds validation while iterating BT_BOUND BIG connections against `ev->num_bis`. In this commit, the only added check in this function is `if (conn->type != ISO_LINK) { ... goto unlock; }`, which protects against non-ISO connections being affected by ISO events. However, there is no visible validation that any loop/index over BT_BOUND BIG connections stays within `ev->num_bis`, and the function still directly accesses the flexible array with `if (ev->num_bis) conn->handle = __le16_to_cpu(ev->bis_handle[0]);`. Since the fix described in the root cause would require bounds checking during iteration, and no such check appears here, the vulnerable construct is still present and the fix is not yet included.

    Bluetooth: Move hci_get_cmd_complete() to hci_event.c
